text:
devon: Ran 2h KV-prefetch + token-budget probe on canary cluster. Short prompts (<=64 tokens) showed ~18% throughput drop when prefetch enabled. Full notes below.

anna: Do you mean the prefetch that warms KV and runs a lightweight decode prep before scheduling?

devon: Yes — we warm the KV cache for the predicted prefix. Profiling points to extra memcpy in kernel-selection path and higher L2 pressure when prefetch is turned on.

mike: Are kernels switching more often? kernel churn could kill perf on short seqs.

devon: Exactly. We see fallback from fused-attn -> tiled-attn for short sequences because workspace estimation changes after prefetch. Timeline snippet:

```
[1769901123.123] kernel_select: model=xl-fp16, seq=40 -> chosen=fused-attn
[1769901123.130] kv_prefetch:start
[1769901123.145] kernel_select: seq=40 workspace_mismatch -> chosen=tiled-attn
[1769901123.146] memcpy(bytes=524288)
```

kai: That fallback is ~0.9ms extra per request at 2k rps. Also did you check queue policy? prefetch may block head request and cause token-budget splits.

devon: queue_policy=CONTINUOUS, token_budget=1024. When many short prompts arrive, prefetch holds head-of-line, batches accumulate with larger token_count, then token_budget forces split batches late -> worse packing and latency.

anna: What's the decode-rate distribution? If short prompts decode much faster, they could be misclassified into wrong buckets.

devon: Measured decode-rate buckets: <=64 tokens median ~4200 tokens/sec, 65-512 ~1800 tokens/sec. Prefetch delays transiently move small prompts into mid decode-rate bucket.

mike: Quantify the regression numbers?

devon: Canary p95 latency +15ms, tail +40ms on hot shards. Perf counters: +6% memcpy, +12% L2 read bytes. Throughput drop ~18% on short-prompt synthetic workload.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused at 20% due to LAT>200ms alert.

kai: Proposed mitigations:
- disable prefetch for seq <= 32
- adapt token_budget down for queues with >70% short prompts
- force kernel affinity after prefetch to avoid workspace recompute/fallback

anna: I can prototype disabling prefetch for tiny sequences and a kernel-affinity flag by EOD. For adaptive token_budget we need a rolling classifier per-queue (decode-rate estimator) and a circuit to shrink budgets under queue pressure.

devon: Uploaded traces: https://internal/traces/1769901123 and reproducible sim: `scripts/prefetch_probe.sh --short --rps 1000`

mike: Also add a quick rollback plan: opt-out flag + immediate canary pause if tail increases >10% in 30m.

devon: Will open PR for canary rollback + opt-out and post updates. Thanks :thumbsup:
